# 1 Samuel Chapter 18 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 161r-161v | **Source Image:** 1SA_018_page_001.jpg, 1SA_018_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And when he had finished speaking to Saul, the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
**2** And Saul took David that day and did not allow him to return to his father's house.
**3** And Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as his own soul.
**4** And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him and gave it to David, along with his garments, and even his sword and his bow and his belt.
**5** And David went out and was successful wherever Saul sent him, so that Saul set him over the men of war. And it was good in the eyes of all the people and also in the eyes of Saul's servants.
**6** And as they were coming home, when David returned from striking the Philistine, the women came out from all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet King Saul with tambourines, with songs of joy, and with three-stringed instruments.
**7** And the women who were celebrating sang to one another, "Saul has struck his thousands, and David his ten thousands."
**8** And Saul was very angry, and this saying displeased him. He said, "They have ascribed to David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed thousands. And what more can he have but the kingdom?"
**9** And Saul eyed David with suspicion from that day on.
**10** And on the next day an evil spirit from God rushed upon Saul, and he raved within his house while David was playing the lyre, as he did day by day. And the spear was in Saul's hand.
**11** And Saul hurled the spear, saying, "I will pin David to the wall." But David evaded him twice.
**12** And Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with him but had departed from Saul.
**13** So Saul removed him from his presence and made him a commander of a thousand. And David went out and came in before the people.
**14** And David had success in all his undertakings, for the LORD was with him.
**15** And when Saul saw that he had great success, he stood in dread of him.
**16** But all Israel and Judah loved David, for he went out and came in before them.
**17** Then Saul said to David, "Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you as a wife. Only be valiant for me and fight the LORD's battles." For Saul thought, "Let not my hand be against him, but let the hand of the Philistines be against him."
**18** And David said to Saul, "Who am I, and what is my life or my father's clan in Israel, that I should be son-in-law to the king?"
**19** But at the time when Merab, Saul's daughter, should have been given to David, she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as a wife.
**20** Now Michal, Saul's daughter, loved David. And when they told Saul, the thing pleased him.
**21** Saul thought, "I will give her to him, that she may be a snare for him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him." So Saul said to David a second time, "You shall now become my son-in-law."
**22** And Saul commanded his servants, "Speak to David in private and say, 'Behold, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you. Now therefore become the king's son-in-law.'"
**23** And Saul's servants spoke these words in the ears of David. And David said, "Does it seem to you a small thing to become the king's son-in-law, seeing that I am a poor man and of no repute?"
**24** And the servants of Saul reported to him, saying, "David spoke such and such words."
**25** Then Saul said, "Thus you shall say to David, 'The king desires no bride-price except a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to take vengeance on the king's enemies.'" For Saul intended to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.
**26** And when his servants told David these words, it pleased David to become the king's son-in-law. And before the time had expired,
**27** David arose and went, along with his men, and struck down two hundred Philistines. And David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full number to the king, that he might become the king's son-in-law. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter as a wife.
**28** And Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David, and that Michal, Saul's daughter, loved him.
**29** So Saul was even more afraid of David. And Saul was David's enemy continually.
**30** Then the commanders of the Philistines came out to battle, and as often as they came out, David had more success than all the servants of Saul, so that his name was highly esteemed.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed on the verse count (30 verses) and narrative structure for this chapter. SOPHIA follows the LOGOS formal-equivalence rendering as the baseline consensus, adopting PNEUMA's phrasing where it demonstrably improves clarity without sacrificing accuracy. Key terms and theological vocabulary were consistently rendered across all three translations.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### Verse 4
- **EMET:** "And-Jonathan-stripped-himself [of]-the-robe that [was] upon-him, and-gave-it to-David, and-his-garments, and-even his-sword, and-even his-bow, and-eve..."
- **LOGOS:** "And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him and gave it to David, along with his garments, and even his sword and his bow and his belt..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Jonathan took off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 7
- **EMET:** "And-the-women-who-played answered and-said, "Saul-has-struck his-thousands, and-David his-ten-thousands.""
- **LOGOS:** "And the women who were celebrating sang to one another, "Saul has struck his thousands, and David his ten thousands.""
- **PNEUMA:** "As they danced, the women sang to one another: "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 8
- **EMET:** "And-it-was-hot to-Saul exceedingly, and-this-word was-evil in-his-eyes, and-he-said, "They-have-given to-David ten-thousands, and-to-me they-have-give..."
- **LOGOS:** "And Saul was very angry, and this saying displeased him. He said, "They have ascribed to David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed thousands. ..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Saul was furious, and this refrain galled him. He said, "They have credited David with tens of thousands, but me with only thousands. What more can he..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 9
- **EMET:** "And-Saul-was eyeing [ʿoyen] David from-that day and-onward."
- **LOGOS:** "And Saul eyed David with suspicion from that day on."
- **PNEUMA:** "From that day on, Saul kept a jealous eye on David."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 14
- **EMET:** "And-David-was prospering [maskil] in-all his-ways, and-YHWH [was] with-him."
- **LOGOS:** "And David had success in all his undertakings, for the LORD was with him."
- **PNEUMA:** "In everything he did, David had great success, because the LORD was with him."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 15
- **EMET:** "And-Saul-saw that he [was]-prospering exceedingly, and-he-was-afraid of-him."
- **LOGOS:** "And when Saul saw that he had great success, he stood in dread of him."
- **PNEUMA:** "When Saul saw how successful David was, he was filled with dread."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 16
- **EMET:** "And-all Israel and-Judah loved David, for he [was]-going-out and-coming-in before-them."
- **LOGOS:** "But all Israel and Judah loved David, for he went out and came in before them."
- **PNEUMA:** "But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them in their campaigns."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 19
- **EMET:** "And-it-was at-[the]-time of-giving Merab, daughter of-Saul, to-David, and-she was-given to-Adriel the-Meholathite for-a-wife."
- **LOGOS:** "But at the time when Merab, Saul's daughter, should have been given to David, she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as a wife."
- **PNEUMA:** "But when the time came for Merab, Saul's daughter, to be given to David, she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah instead."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 24
- **EMET:** "And-[the]-servants of-Saul told him, saying, "According-to-these words David spoke.""
- **LOGOS:** "And the servants of Saul reported to him, saying, "David spoke such and such words.""
- **PNEUMA:** "When Saul's servants reported David's words back to him,"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 29
- **EMET:** "And-Saul-continued to-be-afraid of David yet-more, and-Saul-was an-enemy [of]-David all the-days."
- **LOGOS:** "So Saul was even more afraid of David. And Saul was David's enemy continually."
- **PNEUMA:** "Saul became even more afraid of David. So Saul was David's enemy for the rest of his days."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.

— SOPHIA
